title: Add a Roadmap/TODO section to the command center dashboard
description:
Add a TODO / Roadmap section to the command center dashboard so future ideas for the command center itself have one visible home. Operator (Daniel) wants this section at the top of the dashboard, viewable, and each item should display the full prompt body for the idea it represents.

## Scope of THIS task

- Build the TODO section UI + storage only.
- Seed it with ONE initial item (the prompt block below).
- DO NOT also build the pricing tool itself. That work is what the seeded item describes for future generation; it is out of scope here.

## Requirements

1. **Placement.** The TODO section should be the first thing the operator sees when landing on the dashboard. The existing root (`app/page.tsx`) redirects to `/tasks` — the worker can choose the cleanest integration: either prepend the section to the tasks page, give it its own `/roadmap` route and surface it from the nav, or place a collapsed banner above the task list. Pick what feels native to the existing UI.
2. **Item display.** Each TODO entry shows:
   - A short title.
   - The full prompt body, readable in-place (collapsible OK, but the operator must be able to view the full text without leaving the page or hitting another route).
3. **Persistence.** Store entries on disk to mirror the existing pattern. Suggested: `dashboard/data/todos.json` next to `tasks.json`. Read at minimum via a Next.js API route (e.g., `GET /api/todos`). Write support is nice-to-have but not required for this task — seeding via the JSON file directly is acceptable.
4. **Schema.** Each entry should at least carry: `id`, `title`, `body` (the full prompt, markdown), `createdAt`. Leave room for future fields (e.g., `convertedToTaskId`) but do not implement conversion in this task.
5. **Styling.** Match the existing dashboard. Do not introduce new design systems.

## Initial seed entry

Display this verbatim as the first TODO item. Title: "Pricing tool for raw land".

Body (markdown):

---

# Pricing tool for raw land

Build a tool that estimates a defensible list price for a raw land parcel based on real comparable sales data. Goal: tighten the list-price decision so we can flip deals faster instead of guessing on each lot.

## Inputs
- Property facts (acreage, county/state, zoning, access, utilities, features). Either entered manually or pulled from an existing dashboard property record.

## Behavior
- Fetch comparable sales from a configured comps source (Land.com, LandWatch, county recorder, or scraped marketplace data — operator selects). For each comp, capture: address / parcel, acreage, sale price (or current list price flagged as such), sale date, and the source URL.
- Run a configurable pricing algorithm over the comps. Starting factors: per-acre normalization, location proximity weighting, acreage-tier match (within ±50%), recency decay, feature overlap. Output a single estimated value plus a confidence band.
- The estimated value must be **adjustable** in the UI. The operator can override the algorithm's number, and the override is saved alongside the original estimate so we can later compare algorithm vs. operator judgment.
- Every comp used in the calculation must be displayed in a list, each with a **clickable link** back to the original source page so the operator can verify the data point in one click.
- Persist the final (adjusted) value to the property record so it flows downstream into the ad-builder (which currently takes `comparable_sales` and `asking_price` as free-text inputs).

## Out of scope for v0
- Auto-publishing or auto-pricing without operator review.
- Multi-property batch pricing.

## Open questions to resolve at kickoff
- Which comps source(s) to integrate first? (operator preference)
- Scraping vs. official API vs. manual paste — what's reliable enough to depend on long-term?
- Algorithm weights — exposed as sliders in the UI, or hardcoded with a config file initially?

---

## Acceptance check

- Navigating to the dashboard surfaces the TODO section above (or before) the existing task list.
- The pricing-tool entry is visible and its full body can be read without leaving the page.
- `dashboard/data/todos.json` exists with the seeded entry.
claudeNotes: Built Roadmap/TODO section. New files: dashboard/data/todos.json (seeded with pricing-tool entry), app/api/todos/route.ts (GET endpoint), components/RoadmapSection.tsx (collapsible section + per-item expand). Edited: lib/types.ts (Todo interface), lib/data.ts (getTodos), app/tasks/page.tsx (RoadmapSection prepended above task list). Body renders as whitespace-pre-wrap, matching existing TaskCard pattern. Section open by default, items collapsed by default — click to expand full body.

title: Generate ad: 0.1 ac · Chicot, Arkansas · $1,395
description:
Generate a real-estate ad for this property using the **generate-ad** workflow.

## Property facts
- Location: Chicot, Arkansas
- Acreage: 0.1
- Asking price: $1,395
- Coordinates: 33.1182, -91.2574
- APN: 040-02617-000
- Access: paved
- Utilities on site: power, water, internet
- Utilities notes: Can you tell me about water, septic, and internet for the area?

Read 4 pages, searched the web
Short version: this is an in-town lot, so it’s city water and city sewer — septic doesn’t apply — and internet is better than you’d expect for a Delta town of 1,800, with one real caveat on water quality.

Water — City of Eudora Waterworks

Municipal system, billed by the city (the doxo listing is “City of Eudora Waterworks”). A Pine St lot inside the city limits should have a main at the street; the tap fee and meter deposit come from City Hall, (870) 355-4436 is the number listed for the city.
The system is about 70 years old and has had a rough run. A KATV piece from July 2026 described it as “operating on borrowed time”: brown water complaints for years, a lightning strike that knocked out the controls, and the Arkansas Rural Water Association spending a week restoring service. The fix is funded and underway — a $1.58M ARPA/USDA grant for tank rehab and a new well (the well is done), plus ~$4.4M in Phase II improvements, most of it already disbursed, with completion expected by end of 2026. Honest listing language: “city water at the street; the city is midway through a state-funded system rebuild.”
Sewer — city sewer, not septic

Eudora has a municipal wastewater system (the city has active RFQs for water and wastewater improvements), and an in-town platted lot of 4,356 sq ft would be on it. Arkansas has no minimum lot size for septic, but that’s academic here; the Health Department wouldn’t permit a soil-based system on a lot that small where sewer is available anyway.
What to verify with a single call to City Hall: that the sewer main runs along Pine St in front of Lot 27 (not just the alley or the next block) and the tap fee. In small Delta towns the main sometimes skips a block.
Internet

Swyft Fiber lists Eudora (with Parkdale, Portland, Wilmot) as a Chicot County service area — symmetrical 300 Mbps / 500 Mbps / 1 Gig, no contracts. metadata.utilities_notes:
Can you tell me about water, septic, and internet for the area?

Read 4 pages, searched the web
Short version: this is an in-town lot, so it’s city water and city sewer — septic doesn’t apply — and internet is better than you’d expect for a Delta town of 1,800, with one real caveat on water quality.

Water — City of Eudora Waterworks

Municipal system, billed by the city (the doxo listing is “City of Eudora Waterworks”). A Pine St lot inside the city limits should have a main at the street; the tap fee and meter deposit come from City Hall, (870) 355-4436 is the number listed for the city.
The system is about 70 years old and has had a rough run. A KATV piece from July 2026 described it as “operating on borrowed time”: brown water complaints for years, a lightning strike that knocked out the controls, and the Arkansas Rural Water Association spending a week restoring service. The fix is funded and underway — a $1.58M ARPA/USDA grant for tank rehab and a new well (the well is done), plus ~$4.4M in Phase II improvements, most of it already disbursed, with completion expected by end of 2026. Honest listing language: “city water at the street; the city is midway through a state-funded system rebuild.”
Sewer — city sewer, not septic

Eudora has a municipal wastewater system (the city has active RFQs for water and wastewater improvements), and an in-town platted lot of 4,356 sq ft would be on it. Arkansas has no minimum lot size for septic, but that’s academic here; the Health Department wouldn’t permit a soil-based system on a lot that small where sewer is available anyway.
